newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson's profits up 20 percent. [CORRECTED]
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson's profits up 20 percent. [CORRECTED]

text.p: Johnson & Johnson said Wednesday its profits expanded by 20 percent in the third quarter on increased sales across its entire range of medical and consumer products.
(Corrects profit increase in headline and first paragraph to 20 percent from 14 percent.)
The giant health care products company said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 rose to $750 million, or 56 cents a share, from $623 million, or 48 cents a share.

The company, which sells products in 175 countries, said total revenues climbed 14 percent (corrects from 20 percent) to $5.4 billion from $4.7 billion, although the stronger dollar relative to other currencies decreased sales by 1.8 percent.

"We are pleased with these results that reflect continued strong unit volume growth in our business," Chairman Ralph S. Larsen said in a statement. "Most importantly, the growth is broadly based, ranging from consumer skin care products to life-saving drugs to innovative medical devices that are helping to reduce the cost of health care."

The company said its pharmaceutical sales increased 14 percent, fuelled primarily by strong 23 percent growth in the United States. Those sales were also helped by the company's acquisition of medical device maker Cordis.
Sales of consumer products increased by 8.4 percent overall, with U.S. and international sales up 12 percent and 5 percent, respectively.

Contributing to the growth were the Tylenol analgesic and cold products; Monistat 3 treatment for yeast infection; the Neutrogena line of skin and hair care products and the Nicotrol nicotine patch to help smokers quit.

Johnson & Johnson, which is based in New Brunswick, N.J., said its net income for the first nine months of the year increased 20 percent to $2.3 billion, or $1.75 a share, from $1.9 billion, or $1.50 a share.
Sales for the year to date increased 15 percent to $16.1 billion from $14.0 billion, with the strength of the dollar having a 1.7 percent negative impact on sales.
Johnson & Johnson's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $51.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
